scope: Proposition 7.7 (Weak reach inequality and positive-foot transfer) of the manuscript “A positive resolution of De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight” (preprints/De-Giorgis-conjecture-in-dimension-eight-September-26-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 375 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6c92e90f31e12f32), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Given η0 > 0, the penalty parameters can be chosen, in the order specified above, so that the following holds for all sufficiently large d. The function d is locally semiconcave on Σreg, and the singular part of its distributional surface Laplacian is nonpositive. Almost everywhere, |∇Σd| ≤ CΓ exp{CΓ √ log(K(d) + 1)}. (7.21) At an active non-plateau or diagonal contact, ΔΣd ≤ (1 + η0 + CΓd−γ )a2 d + B |∇Σd|2 d , B ≤ 1 + CΓd−γ . (7.22) If ad is sufficiently small, the same bound can be used with B ≤ η0 + CΓad + CΓd−γ, and then |∇Σd| ≥ cΓ > 0. At an active plateau contact, meaning s ≥ 1 − δ2, one has ΔΣd ≤ G1 ( |H(z)| + HNy (y)+ ) + η0 |∇Σd|2 d , Ny = −e. (7.23) For any measurable choice of such contacts, the positive foot charge can be transferred to y with multiplicity at most one and area factor Jy→z = | det(Id + ℓANy (y))| s ≤ CΓ, d(y) ≤ d(z) = G1ℓ, a(y) + D(y) ≤ CΓ/d(z). (7.24) More precisely, Jy→z ≤ 1 + Cδ2 + Ca(y)ℓ whenever a(y)ℓ is bounded by a sufficiently small fixed constant. The constants and the large-reach threshold are fixed before any later defect threshold, collar scale, or exhaustion radius is chosen.
